I have only this small plot of 0.13 hectares, so I must be careful with every shilling I spend. Chemical fertilizer is too expensive for me to buy from the shop, and the subsidy vouchers are hard to get here in Lindi, so I will not use it. However, I will put whatever manure and compost I can collect from our few goats and chickens onto this plot because the soil here is sandy and needs whatever help it can get. For seed, I will use what I saved from last season — the local nuts grow well enough here. I cannot afford pesticides or herbicides, and there is no water nearby for irrigation, so we depend on the rains. My children and I will do all the work ourselves — planting, weeding, and harvesting — which should take us about 25 days in total across the season. We are too poor to hire anyone to help.
